transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-19
Start time: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Emily Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Laura Black (Pinefield Procurement), Sameer Patel (Pinefield InfoSec), Jin Park (Pinefield Legal)

Summary:
Quick alignment before Pinefield's procurement committee meeting next week. Main topics: final pricing signoff path, DPA exception items, KMS/SSO requirements, and a short technical readout comparing Hosted vs Dedicated deployment economics. Redwood to send pricing spreadsheet, SE to provide short bench notes, customer to confirm legal exceptions and committee timing.

Topics covered:
- Pricing approval workflow and who signs off
- MSA/DPA outstanding redlines (data residency, retention, audit logs)
- Privileged keying / KMS and HSM options
- Deployment choices: Hosted API vs Dedicated GPU (and private VPC) with latency/cost tradeoffs
- SOC2/ISO artifacts and timeline for evidence

Transcript (approx, auto-generated with occasional errors):
[00:00] Emily (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. I think we promised a brief pre-brief today — make sure we're aligned before Laura takes this to procurement.
[00:18] Laura (Pinefield): Yep thanks, Emily. We're tight on time, procurement committee next Tuesday, so want to make sure the DPA/msa picture plus pricing is clear.
[00:31] Marco (Redwood SE): Hi all, Marco here, I'll keep the tech bits short — latency, KV cache, and the Dedicated throughput numbers.
[00:45] Sameer (Pinefield InfoSec): Quick note: InfoSec still needs a KMS flow we can sign off on, HSM or customer-managed key in a private VPC is a preferred pattern.
[01:02] Emily: Understood. We support Redwood Private (VPC) and Dedicated with customer-managed KMS, and we have an escrow/HSM partner option. We'll share the KMS integration doc.
[01:20] Jin (Pinefield Legal): On the DPA, legal has three outstanding asks: retention minimums, subprocessors list, and an audit log SLA. We're trying to avoid broad redlines but need clarity.
[01:40] Speaker 2: (mumbled) The subprocessors list is the big one for us, right.
[02:05] Marco: For the audit logs, we provide token-level traces in the console and can push retention beyond default by request. There's a cost to extended retention — we'll call that out in the pricing sheet.
[02:27] Sameer: Also curious about ephemeral caching — KV cache eviction, any data persist concerns? We need reassurance tokens aren't persisted beyond request lifetime.
[02:45] Marco: Right, KV cache is ephemeral and we have a prefix cache option; it doesn't write back to blob stores. I might have said K V cash in the earlier doc — sorry, transcription glitch — it's KV cache.
[03:10] Emily: On pricing: we outlined hosted per-token model and Dedicated committed capacity. Procurement wants to know the decision path — is it finance or procurement committee that signs the pricing?
[03:30] Laura: Procurement takes the commercial decision but they want finance's nod on unit economics. So we'll probably do a procurement review then final finance approval.
[03:48] Emily: OK good. We'll put an appendix showing month 1 vs steady-state cost with sample throughput. Marco will generate a small bench to show latency for the test prompt set.
[04:15] Marco: I'll run that this week. Quick Q: do you plan to push higher concurrency or keep bursts? That affects batching and unit cost.
[04:32] Laura: Initially low concurrency but predictable traffic; might ramp after launch. So predictable throughput matters.
[04:50] Sameer: Security question — SSO. We require SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning, plus RBAC for console. Can you support SSO into a private control plane?
[05:08] Emily: Yes — Redwood supports SAML and SCIM. For Private deployments we can host the control plane in your VPC and integrate with your IdP.
[05:27] Jin: On the MSA redlines — there was a clause about liability cap tied to monthly fees. We need some language change to align with our legal team's risk profile.
[05:46] Emily: We can discuss liability caps; often that's a negotiation point. For procurement committee they'll want to see proposed redlines and a path to signature.
[06:05] Marco: For Dedicated, note that reserved capacity is monthly commit; we can configure burst capacity. That influences both latency and cost. If you commit, you get better unit price.
[06:22] Laura: Is there a simple chart that shows committed vs pay-as-you-go? Makes the narrative easier for committee.
[06:35] Emily: We'll include that. We'll also surface escape clauses for pilot to production.
[06:50] Speaker 1: (quiet) Is SOC2 Type II ready?
[07:02] Marco: Yes, we're SOC2 Type II plus ISO artifacts available on request. We can provide the SOC2 report under NDA and a summary of controls.
[07:20] Sameer: Great, we'll need a SOC2 package plus the mapping to our control requirements.
[07:36] Jin: About the subprocessors, can you give a current list? Our legal insists on a stable list or notification window for changes.
[07:52] Emily: We'll give the subprocessors list and commit to a 30-day notification window for changes — if that's acceptable.
[08:05] Laura: That should help. On pricing approver, we have a two-step: procurement committee then finance signoff. Procurement wants to see total cost of ownership.
[08:23] Marco: I'll prepare a sample TCO with both Hosted and Dedicated for 12 months. It will factor average request size and token counts.
[08:40] Emily: Also, Jin, we had your DPA redlines last week — we can accept three of the minor items, and we'll flag two with noted exceptions: data residency and audit log retention.
[09:02] Jin: Data residency is a blocker unless we can confirm European data stays in EU regions for EU users. Is that enforceable for hosted?
[09:20] Marco: For Hosted, we can geo-route by policy and keep EU traffic in EU regions. For Private, of course you control physical placement. We'll document routing policies.
[09:38] Sameer: One more on keying: can Redwood support BYOK (bring your own key) into HSM (e.g. AWS CloudHSM) and hold no copy of plaintext keys?
[09:55] Marco: Yes, BYOK is supported for keys via our KMS integrations; we can provide architecture doc. There's an option to do customer-managed keys in the Private control plane.
[10:15] Emily: On billing, what's the expected cadence? Monthly invoices with committed capacity credits applied?
[10:25] Laura: Monthly invoicing preferred. Also, procurement may want a three-month trial before full commit.
[10:40] Emily: We can do a pilot with a short trial and then convert to committed capacity; we'll show the transition path in the pricing doc.
[11:02] Speaker 3: (mumbled) How long to get private control plane up?
[11:15] Marco: Private deployment timeline varies, typically 4-8 weeks depending on network approvals and keying. Dedicated can be faster if using Redwood-hosted infra but with reserved capacity gating.
[11:36] Jin: For MSA redlines, will Redwood accept an audit clause that allows Pinefield to request a third-party audit annually?
[11:52] Emily: We can accept a scoped audit light with NDA and scheduled windows — full third-party audits are usually limited but we can negotiate scope.
[12:12] Laura: If we provide the procurement committee with a concise one-pager on the exceptions and the proposed mitigations, that should be sufficient.
[12:28] Emily: We'll do that. Marco will also include the latency and cost bench one-pager.
[12:45] Marco: Quick technical aside — our runtime supports continuous batching and prefix caching. For your prompt distribution we recommend a quantization and model selection profile. That lowers cost.
[13:05] Sameer: Do you support model pinning and rollback? We need a rollback plan in case of regression.
[13:18] Marco: Yes, model version pinning, canary rollouts, and automatic fallback to a cheaper variant if quality drops — described in the rollout playbook.
[13:36] Jin: A couple of DPA nitpicks — deletion confirmation and certificate of destruction for customer data on request. Can you provide that?
[13:55] Emily: Yes, we can provide deletion confirmation and an export of deletion logs. We'll capture that in the DPA response.
[14:12] Laura: On the pricing committee side, any flex on the liability cap tied to revenue bands rather than monthly fees? That helps legal feel better.
[14:30] Emily: We can discuss a liability cap tied to contract value — that's common. We'll flag options in the commercial terms.
[14:48] Speaker 4: (background noise) Are there any compliance add-ons like extended log retention as paid feature?
[14:58] Marco: Yes, extended log retention and dedicated archival storage are add-ons; they'll be priced in the appendix.
[15:12] Jin: If we accept a limited set of DPA exceptions, we need an SLA for audit log access. Any standard window?
[15:28] Marco: Standard is 48 hours for ad-hoc access; we can commit to a shorter SLO for enterprise plans.
[15:40] Emily: Okay, let's move to the timeline. Laura, when is the procurement committee?
[15:48] Laura: Next Tuesday, 2026-11-23. We need materials Friday EOD to get internal review.
[16:00] Emily: Perfect. So Emily to send pricing and one-pager by Friday EOD (2026-11-20) — note earlier we said 23 but they need it earlier.
[16:18] Marco: I'll have the benchmark doc by Monday (2026-11-22) morning.
[16:35] Sameer: We'll review the KMS flow and get back with any technical blockers by 2026-11-24.
[16:50] Jin: I'll return the DPA exceptions list with comments by 2026-11-25.
[17:05] Emily: Great. Any last minute concerns?
[17:12] Laura: Just one: procurement may ask for a short proof-of-performance test. Can we run a limited pilot?
[17:25] Emily: Yes, pilot is supported. We'll include pilot options and timelines in the doc.
[17:40] Marco: For pilot, recommend a 2-week focused run with a small reserved capacity so we can measure cost/latency.
[17:52] Laura: That should work. We'll aim to confirm pilot scope by Monday.
[18:10] Emily: Ok to recap actions: we'll send pricing deck and one-pager on Friday EOD, Marco sends bench Monday, Jin returns DPA items on the 25th, Laura schedules committee invite.
[18:32] Speaker 2: (agreement) Sounds good.
[18:42] Emily: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email and attach docs.
[18:50] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription imperfections: names sometimes garbled (e.g., K V cash), occasional speaker mislabels like Speaker 2/3. The recording cut had minor hiss at 00:45 and 17:00 but overall intelligible.

Referenced artifacts/links (to be shared after call):
- Pinefield pricing spreadsheet (to be attached by Emily)
- Redwood KMS & Private deployment architecture doc (to be attached by Marco)
- DPA redline summary (to be attached by Emily)
- Bench results spreadsheet (to be attached by Marco)

End of transcript.
